279666e7f03e84c7760e.en: Newtalk News South Korean Defense Minister Kang Sin-chul told a congressional committee on Tuesday that the explosion last week that injured two South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) was confirmed to have been caused by a North Korean mine. He pointed out that this move is a clear violation of the Korean Armistice Agreement and stressed that Pyongyang must take full responsibility and the South Korean military will also take step-by-step measures. The explosion occurred on Sept. 21, south of the military demarcation line in North Korea's demilitarized zone, according to Reuters. Kang said the mines were apparently planted by North Korea during border fortifications in the region and were intended to clarify whether the North had deliberately planted them in the knowledge that South Korean forces would enter the area. South Korea's Ministry of Defense and the United Nations Command subsequently launched a joint investigation and found an additional piece of North Korean-made resin near the explosion site.

(Provided by Taipei City Fire Department) Central News Agency reporter Huang Liyun Fax September 29, 115 Newtalk News (Central News Agency reporter Huang Liyun Taipei 29) Taipei City Fire Department said today that a total of 603 fires occurred in North City from January to July this year, nearly 2 of which were caused by stove cooking, calling on the public to implement the "kitchen fire prevention strategy" of extinguishing fires and regularly cleaning up oil stains. The fire department said in a press release that with the increasing frequency of daily cooking and the arrival of an aging society, kitchen fire safety has become an important issue for home disaster prevention. A total of 603 fires occurred in North City from January to July this year, of which 116 fires (19.2%) were caused by stove cooking.

Treatment is more complex than usual tuberculosis, and the efficacy and side effects should be monitored closely and continuously during treatment. In order to optimize the care of drug-resistant tuberculosis patients and avoid the risk of derivative treatment failure and community transmission, the CDC (hereinafter referred to as the CDC) has established a multi-drug-resistant tuberculosis medical care team (Taiwan MDR-TB Consortium, TMTC team) since 2007, integrating medical, public health, testing, pharmaceutical affairs, nursing and other team resources to provide patient treatment drugs at public expense.
